In [[geometry]], the '''augmented pentagonal prism''' is a polyhedron that can be constructed by attaching an [[equilateral square pyramid]] onto the square face of [[pentagonal prism]]. It is an example of [[Johnson solid]].
[[File:J52 augmented pentagonal prism.stl|thumb|3D model of an augmented pentagonal prism]]

== Construction ==
The augmented pentagonal prism can be constructed from a [[pentagonal prism]] by attaching an [[equilateral square pyramid]] to one of its square faces, a process known as [[Augmentation (geometry)|augmentation]].{{r|rajwade}} This square pyramid covers the square face of the prism, so the resulting polyhedron has four [[equilateral triangle]]s, four [[Square (geometry)|square]]s, and two [[regular pentagon]]s as its faces.{{r|berman}} A [[Convex set|convex]] polyhedron in which all faces are [[Regular polygon|regular]] is [[Johnson solid]], and the augmented pentagonal prism is among them, enumerated as 52nd Johnson solid <math> J_{52} </math>.{{r|francis}}

== Properties ==
An augmented pentagonal prism with edge length <math> a </math> has a surface area, calculated by adding the area of four equilateral triangles, four squares, and two regular pentagons:{{r|berman}}<math display="block"> \frac{8 + 2\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5 + 2\sqrt{5}}}{2}a^2 \approx 9.173a^2. </math>
Its volume can be obtained by slicing it into a regular pentagonal prism and an equilateral square pyramid, and adding their volume subsequently:{{r|berman}}<math display="block"> \frac{\sqrt{233 + 90\sqrt{5} + 12\sqrt{50 + 20\sqrt{5}}}}{12}a^3 \approx 1.9562a^3. </math>

The augmented pentagonal prism has a [[Point groups in three dimensions|three-dimensional symmetry group]] <math> C_{2\mathrm{v}} </math> of order four. It has five [[dihedral angle]]s (an angle between two polygonal faces), obtained by adding the equilateral square pyramid and the regular pentagonal prism's angle. These angles are as follow:{{r|johnson}}
* an angle between two adjacent triangular faces is that of an equilateral square pyramid between two adjacent triangular faces, <math display="inline"> \arccos \left(-\frac{1}{3} \right) \approx 109.5^\circ </math>,
* an angle between two adjacent square faces is the [[internal angle]] of a regular pentagon <math display="inline"> \frac{3\pi}{5} = 108^\circ </math>.
* an angle between a square and a pentagon is that of a regular pentagonal prism between its base and its lateral faces <math display="inline"> \frac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ </math>.
* an angle between pentagon and triangle is <math display="inline"> \arctan \left(\sqrt{2}\right) + \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 144.7^\circ </math>, for which adding the dihedral angle of an equilateral square pyramid between its base and its lateral face <math display="inline"> \arctan \left(\sqrt{2}\right) \approx 54.7^\circ </math>, and the dihedral angle of a regular pentagonal prism between its base and its lateral face.
* an angle between a square and triangle is <math display="inline"> \arctan \left(\sqrt{2}\right) + \frac{3\pi}{5} \approx 162.7^\circ </math>, for which adding the dihedral angle of an equilateral square pyramid between its base and its lateral face, and the dihedral angle of a regular pentagonal prism between two adjacent squares.
